proverb: چپ چپِیتی کم سنوارے
translation: A quiet, silent woman efficiently manages household tasks.

proverb: جنھے لایا گلیں، اودھے نال ٹر چلی
translation: She follows anyone who engages her in smooth talk.

proverb: منہ دی کولی گلاں پٹاوے
translation: A soft-spoken woman invites flirting / flirts with others.

proverb: جے شوہ آکھے فٹے منہ، تاں میں جیواں
translation: When my husband rebukes me, only then do I feel lively/reinvigorated.

proverb: گلاں ولوں میں وڈی، کارتُوتاں وڈی جٹھانی
translation: I am senior in verbal chatter, but my sister-in-law is senior in actual deeds.

proverb: گلیں لگی تے اٹا کتیاں کھادا
translation: She got absorbed in gossip while the dogs ate the flour.

proverb: مرض دا بولیا تے فجر دا گرجیا برتھا نہ جائے
translation: A man's word and the early morning thunder never go to waste.

proverb: مرض دی گل تے گڈی دا پہیا اگے نوں جاندے نے
translation: A man's word and the wheels of a moving vehicle always move forward.

proverb: منہ تے کہوے تاں مرد منو
translation: Consider him a true man who speaks the truth face-to-face.

proverb: قول ہارن جواناں دا کم نہیں
translation: Backing out of one's word is not the trait of real men.

proverb: جہرڑا رن دے آکھے لگے اوہ خراب تھیندا اے
translation: He who follows the advice of his wife is destined to suffer.

proverb: شکل چڑیلوں سی، مزاج پریوں کے
translation: Looks like a witch, but puts on the temperament of a fairy.

proverb: حسین بیوی اور سرحدی قلعہ لڑائی جھگڑے کی جڑ ہیں
translation: A beautiful wife and a border fort are the root of all conflicts.

proverb: جب ناچنے لگی تو گھونگھٹ کیسا
translation: When one starts dancing in public, why wear a veil?

proverb: عورت اور شراب انسان کے ہوش و حواس گم کر دیتے ہیں
translation: Women and wine make a man lose his senses.

proverb: جسے پیا چاہے وہی سہاگن
translation: She whom the husband favors is the true wedded bride.

proverb: چمئار کی جورو ٹوٹي جوتي
translation: The cobbler's wife wears broken shoes.

proverb: برارو لوڑی اسپرارو الوس
translation: See the brother and marry his sister.

proverb: کھونگیر دیاک ژاوَو سار ورنگوشٹی موش جم
translation: An idle husband is better than a warrior son.

proverb: ویسوروتے دودور دی سور ٹوکھیر
translation: Even a lizard may court a widow.

proverb: موش بوکانتے ٹونگ چھانا ژاغا بویئے
translation: A pearl leaf is enough space for a husband and wife.

proverb: تا موش ما موش بول
translation: Your husband and mine together create an army.

proverb: خوش نو استاٰےدنیا نو اوشیا
translation: The world cannot exist without a beloved.

proverb: ژاوٗو اژیکو انوس زور
translation: Stern is the birth of a son.

proverb: ای ادینہ کی گوئے تان ژاٰوو خدایئ دوم
translation: If there were only one Friday, I would gladly sacrifice my son.

proverb: ژور دیتی ژاٗو کرینے
translation: Give a daughter and obtain a son.

proverb: نو استونیرو ژٰاو ژٰاو نو، نو کرینیرو خانہ زاد خانہ زاد نو
translation: A son born without labor pain will be disobedient, and a servant bought free will be disloyal.

proverb: شوم ژاوٗوتے کیا یراغ شوم ژوروتے کیا زیوور
translation: No need to arm an unruly son, and no need to adorn an unruly daughter.

proverb: ہوساک کیمیریو سار وفا نکی ڑینگاک دارو سار
translation: Trust not in a giggling lady nor a quivering wood.

proverb: روشت دنیو سار ڑینگاک دارو سار وا اوساک کیمیریو سار وفا نکی
translation: Place no trust in a bright day, shaking wood, or a laughing woman.

proverb: دورتیک رویو سار بیری نیسیرو گوردوغ جم
translation: A traveling donkey is better than a homebound man.

proverb: ای اوشپوڑو سم غیچ نکی ای ژورو سوم
translation: Neither a tumor nor a daughter has eyes.

proverb: کیمیریو بیچو کوتیر
translation: A woman is a dagger in the chest.

proverb: عورتو شونین دیت سوګونو پھیرین
translation: Win a woman's favor through flattery and a plant through ash fertilizer.

proverb: ای روپیہ سوت استری
translation: Seven wives for one single coin.

proverb: ګون نیکیا وا مہ ژاوٗوت باردوخوتے بوک نو بوئے
translation: Finding a wife for my son is as easy as finding a handle for an axe.

proverb: ای ژور جوش جمار
translation: One daughter attracts ten prospective sons-in-law.

proverb: کوس چوست بوک بوےَ وا کوس ٹون چھونجیر
translation: Some men are blessed with charming wives; others carry tightened slingshots.

proverb: خورو بوک غیچا شیلی
translation: Another man's wife looks beautiful in one's eyes.

proverb: چھانی کی نیسایے بسیرو وایے کام بویے
translation: When the kid is born, the mother goat's market value decreases.

proverb: چستی بیر گلائی بیہچور
translation: Beauty fades, but grievances persist.

proverb: چماچہ چوستی نکی ٹھاشٹا نخرہ
translation: Little beauty, yet endless pretension.

proverb: عورت پھیروانوں بچیں موش میدانوں بچیں
translation: Man for the open field; woman for the domestic hearth.

proverb: عورتو شونګہ ژانگ کولانو ژانگہ
translation: A woman fights her battle in childbed; a man fights his on the battlefield.

proverb: لوٗو لوٹ کوریکو سار دونو لوٹ کو
translation: Better (for a woman) to make a large block of butter than to speak big words.

proverb: چیق کی کیڑیتاٰے نان تو دایئر
translation: The mother feeds her child only when he cries.

proverb: غوٹو لوان غوٹو نان ہوش کوئے
translation: Only a mother understands her mute child's unspoken words.

proverb: جم عورتو غاریہ پتہ بوئے،جم کولانو موسافریہ
translation: A woman's skill is proven in the high pasture; a man's is proven in travel.

proverb: ناقابلو درونګ پیتین
translation: An unskilled woman uses an excessively long thread.

proverb: جنیں پاد ءِ سواس انت۔
translation: The wife is a shoe for the foot.

proverb: برات گوہارانی آہنی پھل انت، پِت جنکانی سایگ انت سردیں، مات جنکانی شگ و آدینک انت۔
translation: A brother is a strong iron wall of protection for sisters; a father is a cool shadow for daughters; a mother is a comb and mirror for girls.

proverb: جنیں شیطان ءِ کدو انت۔
translation: A woman is the nest/abode of Satan.

proverb: برات اگر کور انت، گوہار چمدار انت۔
translation: A sister looks up to her brother for support, even if he is blind.

proverb: گوہار و جن ءِ پاسبان خدا انت۔
translation: God is the ultimate guardian of a wife and a sister.

proverb: جنیں چک نان پہ قسمت وارت۔
translation: A female child gets her food only by luck/destiny.

proverb: جنیں چک مثال ءِ پل اے۔ روچے نہ روچے یکے زرت ئے روت۔
translation: A daughter is like a flower; one day someone will come and pick her away.

proverb: گوہار کہ برات نیست، بزاں کلات ءِ واجہ ئے مان نیست۔
translation: A woman without a brother is like a fortress without a master.

proverb: جنیں ءِ لگام ءَ مرد داریت۔
translation: The reins/control of a woman are in a man's hands.

proverb: جنیں ءِ کور پُر انت بلے نہ تاچیت۔
translation: A woman's river is full, yet it does not flow.

proverb: جنک لاج کنت بہا لک انت، مردیں کہ لاج کنت بہا کاہ انت۔
translation: A shy woman is worth a hundred thousand; a shy man is worth a blade of grass.

proverb: سکی اں برات مرکب اں اوشتان، وشیاں اتونیں جن اوں نوشاں۔
translation: In hardship, brothers stand like riding camels; in happiness, one enjoys with a wife.

proverb: برات ءِ شوڈکیں لاپ سیر بیت، گوہار ءِ سوتکگیں مگونگ درا نبیت۔
translation: A brother's hungry stomach eventually gets filled, but a sister's burnt wound never heals.

proverb: جنیں پہ گپ، مردیں پہ کار۔
translation: Women are for talking, men are for action.

proverb: جنیں ءِ عقل پاد ءِ پونزہ ءَ انت۔
translation: A woman's intellect lies under her heel.

proverb: جنیں چک پہ لوگ ءَ، مردیں چک پہ سیل و ساد۔
translation: A female child is for the house; a male child is for outings and the public sphere.

proverb: جنیں پہ نشگ ءَ، مردیں پہ دیوان ءَ۔
translation: Women are for sitting at home, men are for the public council (dewan).

proverb: جنیں ئے عقل تنگ انت۔
translation: A woman's mind/understanding is narrow.

proverb: جنیں کہ جنوزام بیت، سوچیت و سامان بیت۔
translation: When a woman becomes a widow, she becomes like a burnt object.

proverb: جنیں کاش ءِ گوک نوارث، مرد مکسکے من پگہ تلا انت۔
translation: A woman is like dry grass that even a cow won't eat; a man is a fly sitting proudly on a golden turban.

proverb: جنیں یار ئے شیطان ئے۔
translation: A woman is a friend of the devil.

proverb: جنیں ءَ بپست چو پس ءَ ترا وش نام کنت گوں ہر کس ءَ۔
translation: Feed your wife like a goat and she will praise your name to everyone.

proverb: جنیں کپے بس انت۔
translation: Half a wife was enough.

proverb: جنیں چک چربیں زک ے۔
translation: A female child is like an oily leather skin container.

proverb: جنیں کچنـبکیں پہ گشگ شرکار نبیت۔
translation: A corrupt/stubborn woman cannot be made good by mere advice.

proverb: جنک چو اسک ءَ ببیت، بچک چو شیر ءَ ببیت۔
translation: A girl should be gentle like a deer, a boy should be brave like a lion.

proverb: جنیں کنیزگے، راست ئے کن ئے پروشیت۔
translation: A woman is like a delicate stalk; if you try to force it straight, it breaks.

proverb: دو پاد ءِ مات ءَ شر کن، چار پاد ءِ پِت ءَ۔
translation: Ensure the mother of two feet (human) is good, and the father of four feet (livestock) is good.

proverb: डोहाळ्यावरून मुलाची लक्षणें ओळखावीं
translation: A child's character may be known by the mother's longings (during pregnancy).

proverb: त्याचा बाप तोच
translation: He is his own father. It is a father's duty to punish; here, he is punishing himself by his folly, and therefore is his own father.

proverb: दत्त म्हणून उभा
translation: Adopted therefore he stands forward.

proverb: दरिद्री सार्यांचा मेहुणा
translation: A poor man is brother-in-law of all.

proverb: दादा अंगी वहिनी सोयरी
translation: A brother is one's own flesh, his wife is only a relative.

proverb: दादाची किल्ली वहिनीपाशी
translation: My brother's key is with his wife. She can influence him. Also a similar proverb, Dadaci khoda vahinila mahita (My brother's bad habit is known to my brother's wife).

proverb: दुबळी आई आणि कोरडी नाई
translation: A poor mother is like a dry river.

proverb: नणंद आणि कळींचा आनंद
translation: A husband's sister takes pleasure in mischief.

proverb: नणंद खेळी रहाटाची फळी
translation: A husband's sister is mischievous; she is like the board of a spinning-mill. She sits quietly and sets others quarrelling.

proverb: बापानें मुलाला मारलें तरी वेगळा होत नाहीं
translation: Although the father beat his son they do not separate from each other.

proverb: बेटी बापाची जमीन पादशाहाची
translation: A daughter is her father's (just as) the land is the emperor's. He arranges for her marriage.

proverb: मागून पुढून बापच नवरा
translation: First and last father is the bridegroom. A widower remarrying who does not arrange for his son's marriage.

proverb: लेंक असली परी परी तरी परघरीं जाणारी
translation: Although a daughter be a fairy she will go to a stranger's house, i.e. she will marry.

proverb: व्याह्या जांवयां तुपाचा पेला आणि घरचा पाहुणा उपाशी मेला
translation: A cup of butter to the son-in-law and his father while the guest dies of starvation.

proverb: सोयऱ्यांत साळा हत्यारांत भाला
translation: A brother-in-law among relatives; a spear among weapons. These are good.

proverb: केस ना मेस बोडकीस बेस
translation: Neither hair nor anything yet a widow is attractive.

proverb: कोणाला कशाचें व बोडकीला केसाचें
translation: Some are thinking of their trials, the widow is thinking of her hair.

proverb: बोडकीला कुंकू व वांझेला कातबोळा
translation: Forehead-powder to a widow, and katabola (medicine) to a barren woman. Both useless.

proverb: बोडकें न्हाले आणि पाणी वायां गेले
translation: The widow bathed and the water was wasted. It is useless for a widow to bathe and adorn herself as she has no husband.

proverb: रांड बिंड म्हणा आणि पोटभर वाढा
translation: Call me a widow or what you like but give me enough to eat.

proverb: आपा घर की बाप घर
translation: Her own house or her father's. There is no other place for a married woman.

proverb: आपण नागवी पाहणारे लबाड
translation: She herself is naked (shameless), (yet calls) those who are looking at her wicked.

proverb: एक गोरी बाहत्तर खोडी चोरी
translation: One fair woman (and she has) seventy-two hidden vices.

proverb: एक तिडीक दे आणि घरची धनीण हो
translation: Bear the pain once and become mistress of the house. The wife's position is greatly improved after she has had a son.

proverb: एक पुती रडती दुपुती रडती सातपुती रडती आणि निपुती ती पण रडती
translation: She who has one child cries, she who has two cries, she who has seven cries, and she who has none she also cries. No one is satisfied.

proverb: गौर रुसली सौभाग्य घेऊन बसली
translation: The girl sulked and sat gravely like a married woman.

proverb: जिकडे गेली वांझ तिकडे झाली सांज
translation: Where the childless woman goes there she will stay till evening.

proverb: दुसऱ्याची स्त्री विष वल्ली
translation: Another's wife is a poisonous plant.

proverb: नकटीचे लग्नास सतराशें विघ्नें
translation: There are seventeen hundred objections to a noseless woman's marriage!

proverb: नारीचें बोलणें गवताचें शेकणें
translation: A woman's talk (is like) heat from grass, i.e. it is useless.

proverb: फुकाची बाईल कशाला राहील
translation: A woman who costs nothing; why will she remain? Others will not serve us for nothing.

proverb: बायकांची अक्कल चुलीपाशी
translation: Women's wisdom is connected with the fire-place.

proverb: बायकांचे गाणे आणि नागवे न्हाणे
translation: Women's singing and naked bathing. Both are bad. Respectable women in India do not sing and they bathe in their clothes.

proverb: बायकोचा कावा न कळे ब्रह्मदेवा
translation: Even Bramha does not know the schemings of a woman.

proverb: लावशील लळा तर पडेल गळां
translation: If you show her affection she will fall about your neck.

proverb: स्त्रियांची वर्मे स्त्रियांस माहीत
translation: Women know the foibles of women.

proverb: स्त्रिया साधनानुकूल होत
translation: Women are attracted by rich men. By a slight alteration it may mean 'by riches;' and also, 'Women are subdued by tricks.'

proverb: आपण विणा सवत साहीना
translation: She herself does not bear children and yet she cannot endure a fellow-wife. 'Dog in the manger' spirit.

proverb: एका पुरुषाच्या दोन बायका घरांत किरकिर करूं नका
translation: The two wives of one man, let them not quarrel in the house!

proverb: कागा बाई दुबळी म्हणे निघाले वेगळी
translation: O madam! why are you so thin? 'I have separated from my husband.'

proverb: चांगली बायको जगाची वाईट बायको मनाची
translation: A good-looking wife is the world's, an ugly one is our own.

proverb: जिच्या नवरा दास्यट तिचा संसार चोखट
translation: She manages well whose husband is a slave to her. The Indian wife is generally a good manager if left alone.

proverb: जित्या नाहीं गोडी आणि मेल्या बंधनें तोडी
translation: While he was alive she was not affectionate, now he is dead she breaks her necklaces and bangles.

proverb: जेथें दगड तेथें धगड
translation: Where there is a (husband of) stone there will be a paramour.

proverb: जोरू साथ आणि पैसा गांठ
translation: Tie up and carry with you your wife and your money. Neither should be trusted to the care of another.

proverb: डाग झाला जुना आणि मला पतिव्रता म्हणा
translation: The thing has become old and (says) 'Call me a faithful wife.'

proverb: तरणीचे गाल म्हातारीचे हाल
translation: The young wife's cheeks: the old wife's neglect. He is fond of kissing his young wife.

proverb: तासा आड बैल आणि दिसा आड बायको मारावी
translation: Beat a bullock every other furrow, and a wife every other day. A Shudra proverb. 'A spaniel, a woman, and a walnut-tree, the more they're beaten the better they will be' (English).

proverb: दादल्यापेक्षां बायको मोठी मुसळ घेऊन लागे पाठीं
translation: If the wife be bigger than the husband she will run after him with the pestle.

proverb: नवऱ्याचें मारणें आणि चिखलांत पडणें
translation: A husband's beating is like a fall in the mud. The consequences are soon forgotten.

proverb: नवें नवें जेवी सवें
translation: While new they dine together! Refers to newly-married people. After a time the husband takes his meal first.

proverb: नव्याचे नऊ दिवस मेल्याचे तीन दिवस
translation: Of a new (husband) nine days, of a dead one three days. This is how long a wife's love lasts!

proverb: नव्या नव्या बायकांच्या नव्या नव्या परी पहिली होती ती असें नाहीं करी
translation: New wives have new fancies, the first did not behave so.

proverb: नाजूक नार आणि चाबकाचा मार
translation: A delicate wife and beating with a whip. Perhaps implying that if strong and robust the husband would think twice before beating her.

proverb: नावडतीची आली पाळी गांवाची झाली होळी
translation: The turn of the disliked wife came and the village was set on fire. The man's two wives take turns in cooking. The holi is a pile of wood burnt at the Holi festival.

proverb: नावडतीचें मीठ अळणी आवडतीचा शेंबूड गोड
translation: The salt of the disliked wife is tasteless, the mucus from the nose of the favoured wife is pleasant. The two are wives of one man.

proverb: पतिव्रता नार रात्रीं हिंडे दारोदार
translation: A faithful wife yet she goes from door to door at night.

proverb: पतिव्रता नी मुसळ देवता
translation: A faithful wife or the pestle as a god. (A story is told of a devout wife pounding rice with a long pestle; when her husband called her, she let go of the raised pestle to obey him, and it stayed suspended in the air, proving her faithfulness. Another wife, hoping for the same fame, tried the same trick, but the pestle fell and bruised her head. Now applied to one who boasts of her faithfulness, with the reply: 'A faithful wife! yes, or else the pestle is your god.')

proverb: फिरली नार तर भ्रतार मार
translation: If the woman turn on her husband she may kill him.

proverb: बायकांना लोण्याची सवतही सहन होत नाहीं
translation: Women cannot endure a fellow-wife even if she be (soft as) butter.

proverb: बायको दुसरी फजिती तिसरी
translation: A second wife; disgraceÊ a third thing. The two wives will quarrel and bring disgrace.

proverb: म्हातारा दादला जिवाला आधार
translation: An old husband is a support to life. Or, perhaps better, kunkumala adhar (an excuse for using the forehead mark), i.e. it shows that she is a wife, not a widow.

proverb: शिळी भाकर ताकानें गोड व वाईट बायको पोरानें गोड
translation: Stale bread is sweet with butter-milk and a bad wife becomes sweet when she has a child.

proverb: स्त्रियाचा जीव पती
translation: The husband is the life of the woman.

proverb: कशी गे सुने घरासारखी
translation: O daughter-in-law! why are you behaving so? (She answers) 'Like the household.'

proverb: कानाला कोंपर झडेना सासू मेली जांवई रडेना
translation: The elbow will not touch the ear and the son-in-law will not cry when his mother-in-law dies.

proverb: गांवचा गांढ्या पण सासवेचा देशपांड्या
translation: A fool in the village but a lord in the opinion of his mother-in-law.

proverb: चार दिवस सासूचे चार दिवस सुनेचे
translation: Four days of the mother-in-law's (authority) and four days of the daughter-in-law's. The latter asserts her authority when she has children.

proverb: पोराला पंतोजी व पोरीला सासू
translation: A teacher for a boy,Ê a mother-in-law for a girl. The one is the equivalent of the other.

proverb: बोले धुवे लागे सुने
translation: Whether talking or cleaning (the pots) it affects the daughter-in-law. Whatever the mother-in-law says or does is intended to reprove the daughter-in-law. If dhuva means 'daughter' (Molesworth) then the proverb would be, 'What is said to the daughter is meant for the daughter-in-law.'

proverb: माहेरचें सुख सासरीं होतें दुःख
translation: (The girl feels) happiness at home but pain at her mother-in-law's.

proverb: लेंकीस बोले सुनेस लागे
translation: What is said to the daughter is meant for the daughter-in-law. So that the girl may not complain to her mother or her husband, the sasu addresses her own daughter, urges her to work, chides her for laziness, etc., but all the time she intends it for her daughter-in-law. The first words may be kombadisa bole (What is said to the fowls).

proverb: वेडीला सासर काय आणि माहेर काय
translation: What is a mother-in-law's house or a mother's house to a mad woman? She would be mad indeed not to know the difference.

proverb: सावत्र आई विषय जाई
translation: A step-mother, and no enjoyment.

proverb: सासरीं जातां कुचकुच कांटे माहेरीं येतां हरीख वाटे
translation: She walks on thorns to her mother-in-law's, but she feels delight in coming to her mother's house.

proverb: सासवेचे दोंदावर जांवई उदार
translation: The son-in-law is liberal with the distended paunch (property) of his mother-in-law.

proverb: सासू गेली ठीक झालें घरदार हातीं आलें
translation: I am glad mother-in-law has gone (is dead), the whole house is now in my hands. The last phrase is also quoted tupatse gadage hati ale (the butter-pot has come into my charge).

proverb: सासूचा पाय सुनेला लागला सुनेचा पाय सासूला लागला तरी सुनेनेच पाया पडावें
translation: If the mother-in-law's foot knock against the daughter-in-law, or if the daughter-in-law's foot knock against the mother-in-law, it is the daughter-in-law who must beg pardon.

proverb: सासूची वाईट खोड नवरा व मी असले गोड मग इला येतो फोडा
translation: Mother-in-law's bad habit; she hates my husband to be kind to me.

proverb: सासूपणा आला म्हणजे सूनपणाचा जाच विसरते
translation: On becoming a mother-in-law the torments of being a daughter-in-law are forgotten.

proverb: सासूमागें सून नाचे
translation: The daughter-in-law must dance to the mother-in-law's tune.

proverb: सासूला मार आणि सुनेला धाक
translation: Beat the mother-in-law and the daughter-in-law will be afraid.

proverb: सासू सांजोऱ्या तळे माझा जीव जळे
translation: Mother-in-law is making cakes: may my soul be burnt, i.e. I need not expect to get any.

proverb: सुनेला दडपण सासू
translation: The mother-in-law is a check on the daughter-in-law.

proverb: अशी लेंक हवई घरोघर जांवई
translation: A daughter so fair; a son-in-law from every house. All will want to marry her. Another similar saying is Asa lenka dana gharoghara suna (A son so good; a daughter-in-law from every house).

proverb: असतील बाळ तर फेडतील काळ
translation: If there be sons they will prevent misfortune.

proverb: असत्याचा बाप नसत्याची आई
translation: A father for the profitable son, a mother for the unprofitable. 'In prosperity, a father; in adversity, a mother' (Hindustani).

proverb: आईच्या लाडामुळे मूल होई खुळें
translation: By the mother's petting the child becomes an idiot.

proverb: आपलें तें बापडें दुसऱ्याचें तें कातडें
translation: Our own child is tender, another's is (as tough as) leather. Or the last word may be karate (an urchin). Sometimes the two rhyming words are gojiravane (graceful) and laziravane (graceless). 'Every man thinks his own geese swans' (English).

proverb: खायाला आजी करायाला शेजी
translation: A grandmother at eating, a neighbour at working. One ready to eat who keeps away when there is work.

proverb: जांवई शोध
translation: A son-in-law search. He is petted and feasted when he visits his wife's relatives.

proverb: ఆడదానిచేతి అర్థమూ మొగవానిచేతి బిడ్డా బ్రతకదు
translation: Money left in the hands of a woman wont last; a child left in the hands of a man wont live.

proverb: ఆడదాని మాట నీళ్ల మూట
translation: A woman's word, a bundle of water. (A woman's mind and winter wind change oft.)

proverb: ఆడది బొంకితే గోడ పెట్టినట్లు మొగవాడు బొంకితే తడిక కట్టినట్లు
translation: If a woman lies, it's like building a wall; if a man lies, it's like putting up a mat (easily seen through).

proverb: ఆడ పైత్తనము తంబళి దొరతనము
translation: Woman's rule, a Tambali's government. (A Tambali is a Saiva priest of low origin, who wears the sacred thread and endeavours to observe Brahminical customs.)

proverb: బుషిమూలము నదీమూలము స్త్రీ మూలము విచారించకూడదు
translation: Enquire not into the origin of a Rishi, a river, or a woman.

proverb: కడవంత గుమ్మడికాయ అయినా కత్తిపీటకు లోకువ
translation: Although the pumpkin be as big as a large pot, yet it is subject to the kitchen knife. However great a family a wife may come from, she must still be subject to her husband.

proverb: కుట్టిన తేలు గుణవంతురాలు కూశినమ్మ కుక్క ముండ
translation: The scorpion which stung is a good tempered creature, the [stung] woman who bawled out is a wretched slut. (A mischief maker often escapes blame.)

proverb: కులమింటి కోతి అయినా మేలు
translation: A monkey [-like wife] of good family is better [than a pretty wife of low origin].

proverb: తల్లిని చూచి పిల్లనూ పాడిని చూచి బర్రెనూ తీసుకోవలెను
translation: Look at the mother before you take the daughter; see how much milk the buffalo gives before you buy her.

proverb: నవ్వే ఆడదాన్ని ఏడ్చే మొగవాన్ని నమ్మరాదు
translation: A laughing woman and a crying man should not be trusted.

proverb: మున్నూరు శిఖలయినా కూడ వచ్చునుగాని మూడు కొప్పులు కూడ రాదు
translation: Three hundred Sikhas (i.e. men) may come together, but three Koppus (i.e. women) should not get together. (Sikha is the top-lock worn by men and Koppu is a woman's chignon.)

proverb: మొయిలు విడిచిన యెండ మొగుడు విడిచిన ముండ పట్టి విడిచిన మండ రెత్తి విడిచిన కుండ తీక్ష్ణము
translation: The heat of the sun emerging from the clouds—the passion of a meretricious woman separated from her husband—the violence of a bough bent and let go—the force of a pot lifted up and dropped—are great. ("Give the water no passage; neither a wicked woman liberty to gad abroad." Ecclesiasticus xxv. 25.)

proverb: రంకాడనేర్చినమ్మ బొంకాడనేరదా
translation: Will the woman who has learnt to play the harlot, not learn to lie?

proverb: లంజకు పిల్ల తఖలాటము
translation: A child is a hindrance to a harlot.

proverb: లంజ చెడి యిల్లాలు అయినది
translation: The changed harlot became an honest woman. (Ironical.) Chastity gone once, gone for ever.

proverb: లంజ బిడ్డకు తండ్రి యెవరు
translation: Who is the father of a harlot's child?

proverb: వెర్రివాడి పెండ్లాము వాడవదినా
translation: A madman's wife is common property. (The helpless are mocked and ill-treated.)

proverb: తల్లి చేసినది తనయులకు
translation: What a mother does, [falls] on her children. (If she sin, her children are disgraced.)

proverb: బహునాయకం బాలనాయకం స్త్రీనాయకం
translation: Having many leaders, having a youthful leader, having a female leader (Is equally bad). (Said of people, an army, etc.)

proverb: अनायका विनश्यन्ति नश्यन्ति शिशुनायकाः। स्त्रीनायका विनश्यन्ति नश्यन्ति बहुनायकाः॥
translation: Those without a leader perish; those with a youthful leader perish; those with a female leader perish; those with many leaders perish.

proverb: आत्मबुद्धिस्सुखं चैव गुरुबुद्धिर्विशेषतः। परबुद्धिर्विनाशाय स्त्रीबुद्धिः प्रलयंकरी॥
translation: One's own resolve is happy, the priest's advice is better; another's advice is for one's ruin, woman's counsel is destructive.

proverb: उत्तमं स्वार्जितं वित्तं मध्यमं पित्रार्जितम्। अधमं भ्रातृवित्तं च स्त्रीवित्तमधमाधमम्॥
translation: [To live upon] self-acquired property is good, [to live upon] that acquired by a father is middling, [to live upon] a brother's property is low, [to live upon] a woman's property is the lowest of the low.

proverb: औदुंबराणि पुष्पाणि श्वेतवर्णं च वायसं। मत्स्यपदं जले पश्येन्नारीहृदयस्थितं॥
translation: The flowers of the fig tree, a white-coloured crow, a fish's foot in the water, one may see—but not what is in a woman's mind.

proverb: कदलीवंध्या काकीवंध्या॥
translation: Barren as a plantain, barren as a crow. (A woman who has one child and then dies is like the plantain which produces one bunch and then perishes; a woman who brings forth once and is afterwards barren is like the crow which lays eggs but once.)

proverb: कार्येषु दासी करणेषु मंत्री रूपे च रंभा क्षमया धरित्री। भोज्येषु माता शयने तु वेश्या षड्धर्मयुक्ता खलु धर्मपत्नी॥
translation: In work, a slave; in business, a minister; in form a Rambha; in patience, [like] the earth; in [providing] food, a mother; in conjugal enjoyments, a courtesan:—is not she who possesses these six qualities, a dutiful wife?

proverb: कोकिलानां खरो रूपं पातिव्रत्यं तु योषितां। विद्या रूपं विरूपाणां क्षमा रूपं तपस्विनां॥
translation: The voice is the beauty of cuckoos; chastity is the beauty of women; learning is the beauty of the deformed; patience is the beauty of ascetics.

proverb: तस्करस्य वधो दंडो दासीदंडस्तु मुंडनं। भार्यादंडः पृथक्कुर्या मित्रदंडस्त्वभाषणं॥
translation: Death is the punishment of a robber, the punishment of a harlot is shaving the head; separation is the punishment of a wife, the punishment of a friend is not speaking to him.

proverb: दिवा काकत्रासिता॥
translation: In the daytime she was frightened by the cawing of a crow. (The feigned timidity of a loose woman.)

proverb: न स्त्री स्वातंत्र्यमर्हति॥
translation: A woman is not fit for independence.

proverb: नारीणां भूषणं पतिः॥
translation: A husband is the ornament of women.

proverb: पिता च ऋणवान् शत्रुर्माता च व्यभिचारिणी। भार्या रूपवती शत्रुः पुत्रश्शत्रुरपण्डितः॥
translation: A father in debt is an enemy [to his son]; a mother of bad conduct is an enemy [to her son]; a beautiful wife is an enemy [to her husband]; an unlearned son is an enemy [to his parents].

proverb: पितृदुःखं तु षण्मासं मातृदुःखं तु वत्सरः। भार्यादुःखं पुनर्भार्या पुत्रदुःखं निरंतरं॥
translation: Sorrow for [the loss of] a father [lasts] six months; sorrow for a mother, a year; sorrow for a wife until a second wife [comes]; sorrow for a son, for ever.

proverb: पुरुषाणामभावेन सर्वा नार्यः पतिव्रताः॥
translation: In the absence of men, all women are chaste.

proverb: पुस्तकं वनिता वित्तं परहस्तगतं गतं। अथवा पुनरायाति जीर्णं भ्रष्टं च खंडशः॥
translation: A book, a woman, or money, when gone into the hand of another, is gone [indeed]; or it returns worn out, corrupted, or by bits.

proverb: बद्धमूलस्य मूलं हि महद्वैरतरोः स्त्रियः॥
translation: Women are the great root of the firmly-rooted tree of enmity. ("Women and dogs set men together by the ears." "A woman's vengeance knows no bounds." — German.)

proverb: दुर्जनं काञ्चनं भेरीं दुष्टस्त्रीं दुष्टवाहनं। इक्षुखण्डान् तिलाश्च्छूद्रान् मर्दयेदुत्तरोत्तरे॥
translation: A bad man, gold, a drum, a bad woman, a bad horse, stalks of sugar cane, sesamum seed, and Sudras should be beaten to improve their qualities. ("A spaniel, a woman and a walnut tree, the more they be beaten, the better they be.'')

proverb: मातृहीनं भृशं जीवं तथा कान्तहीनं नवयौवनं तथा। शांतिहीनं तपः फलं तथा तिंत्रिणीरसविहीनभोजनं॥
translation: Vain is the life of a motherless child, so is the prime [of a woman] without a husband; penance without quietism is fruitless, so is food without tamarind juice.

proverb: कुग्रामवासः कुजनस्य सेवा कुभोजनं क्रोधमुखी च भार्या। मूर्खस्य पुत्रो विधवा च कन्या विनाग्निना संदहते शरीरं॥
translation: Residence in a hamlet, service under a low fellow, coarse food, an ill-tempered wife, a stubborn son, and a widowed virgin [daughter] burn the body without fire.

proverb: राजा राष्ट्रकृतं पापं राजपापं पुरोहितः। भर्ता च स्त्रीकृतं पापं शिष्यपापं गुरुर्भजेत्॥
translation: The king must answer for his country's sin; the priest for the king's sin; the husband for the wife's sin, and the Guru for the disciple's sin.

proverb: लज्जा स्त्रीभूषणं॥
translation: Modesty is the ornament of women. ("I will therefore that ... women adorn themselves ... with shamefacedness." 1 Timothy ii. 8, 9.)

proverb: वृद्धा नारी पतिव्रता॥
translation: An old woman, a chaste wife.

proverb: वृद्धा वेश्या तपस्विनी॥
translation: An old harlot, a female devotee.

proverb: स्त्रियाश्चरितं पुरुषस्य भाग्यं देवा न जानंति कुतो मनुष्याः॥
translation: The gods know not a woman's conduct and a man's fortune, how then can men?

proverb: स्त्रियो मूलमनर्थानां॥
translation: Women are the cause of mischief.

proverb: स्त्रीणां द्विगुणमाहारो बुद्धिश्चापि चतुर्गुणा। साहसं षड्गुणं चैव कामोऽष्टगुण उच्यते॥
translation: Women are said to eat twice as much [as men], to have four times as much sense, six times as much pluck, and eight times as much desire.

proverb: ગાય લેવી દુઝતી, વહુ લેવી શોભતી.
translation: Take a cow that gives milk; take a daughter-in-law (bride) who is beautiful. (Choosing a bride is likened to choosing livestock — for her looks/usefulness.)

proverb: ન મળી નારી એટલે સહેજે થાવા બ્રહ્મચારી. વૃદ્ધા નારી પતિવ્રતા.
translation: Not finding a wife, one easily becomes celibate. An old woman is [naturally] a chaste wife. (Implies a woman's fidelity is only assured once she is old and no longer desired.)

proverb: આદિ વેર ઘંટી તે ઘઉં, આદિ વેર સાસુ તે વહુ.
translation: Primordial enmity [exists] between the grindstone and the wheat; primordial enmity [exists] between mother-in-law and daughter-in-law. (Listed alongside cat-and-mouse, thief-and-honest-man as a 'natural,' inevitable enmity.)

proverb: નારી ઘરનું નાક છે, નારી સુત દેનાર; નારીથી પંખાય છે, નારી સુખ આધાર. નારી વિનુ નિંદાય છે, નારી વિનુ નહીં સુખ; નારી વિનુ નહીં આભરણ, નારી વીસારો દુઃખ.
translation: The wife is the honor ('nose') of the home; the wife is the giver of sons; through the wife one flourishes; the wife is the foundation of happiness. Without a wife one is disgraced; without a wife there is no happiness; without a wife there is no ornament; without a wife there is no forgetting of sorrow. (A woman's value is defined entirely through what she provides a husband/household, not as a person in her own right.)

proverb: પરનારી તાતી છરી, નિત નિત કાપે કાય; જેના રહ્યા રામછ, તે પરનારી ઘર જય. પરનારી પ્રત્યક્ષ દેખો, વીખ હળાહળ અંગ; રાવણનાં દશ શિષ ગ્યા, પરનારી સંગ.
translation: Another man's wife is a hot knife, constantly cutting the body; [only] one who keeps to Ram [avoids] going to another's wife's house. See another's wife as pure poison in the flesh; Ravana lost his ten heads through [involvement with] another's wife.

proverb: પીયા રંગ રાતી રહે, જગસે રહેત ઉદાસ; પીયા ચહા કે મત ચહા, મેં તો પીયહી દાસ. આજ્ઞાકારી પીયહી, રહે પીયહ સંગ; તનમનસેં સેવા કરે, ઓર ન દુજે રંગ. પતિવ્રતાકે તન નહીં, સુરત બસે પીય મન. પતિવ્રતા પતિકુ ભજે, કળહુ નામ નહીં લેત.
translation: She stays dyed in the color of her beloved, indifferent to the world; whether he desires her or not, she remains his servant. Obedient to her husband, she stays by his side; serves with body and mind, taking on no other color [loyalty]. The devoted wife has no [awareness of her own] body — her whole being dwells in her husband's mind. The devoted wife worships her husband, yet never [dares to] speak his name aloud. (The book's closing section, prescribing a wife's total self-erasure and obedience as virtue — including the old taboo against a wife ever saying her husband's name.)
